title: vidIQ MCP: Setup, Credits, Pricing (2026 Guide)
summary: VidIQ MCP gives Claude or ChatGPT access to YouTube analytics for research. It's a data lookup tool, not automation that takes actions on your behalf.
body_markdown:
## VidIQ MCP requirements and costs


Since the vidIQ MCP's available on every vidIQ tier, the real purchase is the monthly credit allowance, which runs from 150 on Free to 6,000 on Max. Prices below were checked on 18 November 2026.


### VidIQ plan and limits


At the low end, Free gets[150 credits a month, Pro 1,000, Boost 2,000 and Max 6,000](https://support.vidiq.com/en/articles/13928456-features-credits-by-plan) . The jump from Free to Pro is nearly sevenfold.


At 150, a few research sessions can drain the month, so Free's a trial, not a workflow. The table puts those allowances next to what each plan costs, plus the chat subscription you pair it with.


Plan Price MCP credits per month


vidIQ Free $0 150


vidIQ Pro Paid tier 1,000


vidIQ Boost $19/mo ($16.58/mo billed yearly) 2,000


Claude Free $0 None; uses your vidIQ credits


ChatGPT Free $0 None; uses your vidIQ credits


ChatGPT Go $8/mo None; uses your vidIQ credits


If your vidIQ allowance is running dry, upgrading ChatGPT won't stretch it. The AI plans add no credits of their own.


Claude Free and ChatGPT Free both cost $0, while ChatGPT Go costs $8 a month, so only the free tiers are directly comparable at no cost.


Before you pay for anything, open your chat app's settings and confirm that your plan lists connectors. That check takes a minute and decides whether the Go upgrade's needed at all.


### Total monthly vidIQ MCP cost for solo creators


Pair Boost with a free Claude or ChatGPT account and it comes to $19 a month, or $16.58 if you pay yearly, so annual payment saves roughly $29 per year.


Add ChatGPT Go and it's $27 monthly, or $24.58 with yearly vidIQ billing, putting the total bundle at $8 more monthly than Boost alone, which means ChatGPT Go effectively costs $8/month when bundled. Those are the realistic figures for one person who wants 2,000 credits.


Only if you actually hit the Boost ceiling do Max's 6,000 credits, triple Boost's, pay off. So the question is simple: does the time you save by not switching between vidIQ tabs and your chat window add up to more than $19 a month?


If the same question gets asked every week, Activepieces covers the repeating part: a flow can run every Monday and post a weekly research summary to Slack.


It sits next to vidIQ rather than in place of it, and no vidIQ integration is part of that, so the vidIQ figures still reach the summary through you or the connector.


What carries over is the connector idea itself: once a piece is connected in Activepieces, an agent can call it, because the same piece runs as a flow step and as a tool on the per-project MCP server that Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor connect to.


Nothing gets published or wired up a second time, and you can see it in packages/pieces of the MIT-licensed repo, which holds 750 integrations, roughly 60% of them community-contributed, so community developers maintain the majority of integrations.
